findings.reason: the clip deliverable would be restated as extending `_traced_clip` and its moment output rather than authoring a new packed clip, which changes the implementing worker's first step.
findings.text: the design says to build "a single clip ... cell geometry entering as DATA ... fixed shapes, vertex counts and supports padded to a capacity", but `nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py::_traced_clip` already pads every support to a fixed `support_capacity`, already takes `cell_vertex_count` and `participating_cell` as data, and is already used by the hex path (`nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:3417`) and the rectangular path (`nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_extraction.py:2039` via `_regular_cell_mesh`, four-vertex cells), so a rebuild forks the one clip the plan exists to keep singular

findings.reason: naming the moment owner keeps the unification an extension of one routine instead of a third parallel moment path beside `fixed_profile_current_moments` and `clipped_support_current_moments`.
findings.text: the one moment method is proposed without naming the existing moment owners `nova/equilibrium/clip_quadrature.py` (`clipped_support_current_moments`, `clipped_support_quadrature`, `saddle_wedge_current_moments`) and `nova/equilibrium/stencil_mesh.py::fixed_profile_current_moments`, even though the plan's own exact-participation followup outcome edits those very routines

findings.reason: the named owners already carry the polygon route the plan wants for hex, so the honest change is an extension of `extraction_lattice.evaluate_forward_equilibrium` / `extract_flux_surface_geometry`, not a parallel extraction path.
findings.text: the extraction half ("flux properties ... extractable from a hexagonal mesh. Current support extractable on a rectangular grid") proposes new extraction machinery without naming `nova/equilibrium/flux_surface_extraction.py::extract_flux_surface_geometry` (the structured-flux-map flux-surface-geometry owner) or `nova/equilibrium/extraction_lattice.py` (the affine extraction-lattice owner, whose `GreenSourceRepresentation` already accepts `analytic_polygon` general polygonal sections via `polygon_analytic_flux_moments`) as the owners to extend

findings.reason: the single-operator claim is false at the partition boundary unless the unification extends `cell_partition_geometry` as well, so the plan would add it to the clip deliverable's scope.
findings.text: the locked decision's "one code path, no host-side dispatch on cell geometry" is contradicted at the partition seam by `nova/equilibrium/cell_partition.py:123::cell_partition_geometry`, which dispatches on tiling (`_tensor_product_axes` raster adapter for tensor-product centroid lattices versus authored six-neighbour rings for the hex carrier), and the plan does not name this owner as part of the unification

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one fixed-shape clip-and-moment operator hides the clip, both cell geometries and the moment quadrature behind one interface, consolidating the existing clip-and-moment surface rather than spreading it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the extraction half proposes hex flux-property extraction without naming the existing extraction owners to extend, and the one-code-path claim is contradicted by an existing per-tiling dispatch the plan does not name.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the design re-describes as new work the capacity-padded geometry-as-data clip that already exists as `nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py::_traced_clip` and is already shared by both tilings, and the existing moment owners are named only in a comment, not in the design.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the design extends the existing shared clip and coupling; the locked decision (same order, accuracy and speed, no runtime adaptation) is a stated reason not to add a per-tiling wrapper.
